sampling_model.design: Three-arm randomized experiment with known assignment probabilities \(\pi_d\).
sampling_model.units: Independent units with the potential efficacy and toxicity components mapped by \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\) to an ordinal response triple supported on \(\mathcal U_L\).
sampling_model.treatment: Observed dose \(A\in\{0,1,2\}\) and observed prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score \(Y=Y(A)\).
sampling_model.overlap: \(\min_{d\in\mathcal D}\pi_d>0\), with realized empty arms handled by the exact fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Arm-specific multinomial probabilities \(p_{dj}\) are estimated by randomized-arm empirical frequencies; exact inference conditions on realized arm counts.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Discrete causal bounds can be computed as polynomial programs with convergent anytime outer bounds.
Finite causal response-type models can have complete observable facet inequalities beyond Pearl's basic instrumental inequality.
A deterministic parent map supports duplicate-free reverse-search enumeration without storing visited objects.

Two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities have sharp cumulative formulas for unrestricted bivariate potential-outcome couplings; those formulas do not transfer sharply to the three-way non-valley support restriction.
Two-potential-outcome distributional bounds under support restrictions admit a Kantorovich-dual characterization.

Unrestricted multiple-potential-outcome identification admits a multi-marginal transport formulation, with a plug-in rate for the paper's quadratic objective; without an extended-cost constrained reduction it gives only inclusion-based outer bounds for the present forbidden-support indicator target.
General potential-response support restrictions have sharp graph-based observable implications, with extra inequalities in nonregular cases.
Randomly perturbed LP value functions yield uniformly valid confidence sets for linear functionals of set-identified parameters.
For Gaussian first-stage limits, ordinary bootstrap consistency is equivalent to full differentiability, and a derivative-estimation bootstrap handles directional maps.
Intersection bounds admit adaptive inequality selection and Gaussian-process inference.
Continuous functionals of the joint distribution of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model admit sharp bounds through random-set restrictions and convex optimization.

For binary treatment and an ordinal outcome, exact randomization inference in the paper assumes independent potential outcomes and concerns the relative treatment effect, not the present three-dose unique-best endpoint map.

Sharp symbolic ordinal bounds are derived for binary-exposure observational confounding and binary-instrument noncompliance designs; they do not classify or evaluate a three-dose forbidden-support unique-best polytope.

body.tldr: Randomization identifies the three marginals of a prespecified ordinal benefit-risk score but not the population shares for which each dose is uniquely best. Under weak individual unimodality, the compatible target vectors form a structured three-marginal polytope. The central open question is whether every primitive facet of this polytope admits a finite geometric predecessor type and is generated exactly once by one fixed, oracle-free, sixteen-register two-pass triangular-affine stream. A positive answer gives an analytic all-support facet catalogue and a fixed transfer recurrence; the resulting catalogue yields sharp endpoint formulas using at most three full facets, endpoint-attaining latent mixtures, and a route to exact support-aware simultaneous inference that becomes scalar efficient on separated positive-support faces. The psilocybin example is only an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis: randomization identifies score marginals, whereas the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality.

project_justification.gap: Russell (2021) sharply bounds continuous functionals of the joint law of two potential outcomes in a binary-treatment model, Chiba (2017) bounds and develops randomization inference for \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\) with two ordinal potential outcomes, and Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic ordinal-benefit formulas in two-arm designs. Generic discrete causal optimizers and multi-marginal transport solvers return numerical values. None classifies the primitive supporting inequalities of the three-dose non-valley coupling polytope for every finite ordinal support, proves a finite predecessor calculus, or compiles such a calculus into an exact-once bounded-register stream; the three-facet endpoint result addresses a unique-best indicator whose forbidden-support geometry is invisible in every two-arm projection.
project_justification.niche: The non-valley support is genuinely three-way: every two-coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U_L\) is the unrestricted square \(\mathcal Y_L^2\), even though the full support deletes triples with \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\). The first new step is therefore minimization of candidate affine slack over that non-Cartesian three-marginal support, followed by tight-row rank classification. Pairwise Hall inequalities and regular compatibility-graph arguments miss weighted full facets, while generic hull enumeration does not explain the observed staircase, doubling, and Fibonacci coefficient families.
project_justification.fill: The project isolates tight-product extremizer and rank signatures, seeks a finite renormalized predecessor classification, and requires a literal \(\texttt{CHECK\_2BTAS}\)-accepted source whose soundness, completeness, and uniqueness are mathematical claims. The same representation is then projected to sharp unique-best endpoints and coupled to exact multinomial inference with an explicit regular-face efficiency target.

body.related_work: Russell (2021) studies continuous functionals of the joint distribution of the two potential outcomes \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) in a binary-treatment model, using random-set core-determining restrictions and convex optimization to obtain sharp bounds; that general two-potential-outcome method informs the optimization layer but does not classify a three-marginal forbidden-support polytope. Chiba (2017) studies the binary-treatment ordinal relative-treatment-effect parameter \(P\{Y(1)\ge Y(0)\}\), gives numerical sharp nonparametric sample bounds, and develops exact randomization inference under an independent-potential-outcomes assumption; its response type is likewise a pair \(Y(0),Y(1)\). Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018) derive cumulative sharp bounds and attaining tables for two-arm ordinal benefit probabilities; their construction motivates the endpoint layer but does not cover a three-way forbidden support. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024) derive sharp symbolic formulas for ordinal measures of benefit, no harm, and relative treatment effect for binary exposure under confounding and for binary-instrument noncompliance settings; those formulas concern two potential outcomes, whereas \(\text{thm:sharp-three-facet-endpoints}\) targets the unique-best indicator among three potential outcomes under a forbidden-three-way-support restriction and can require three full-facet normals. The first genuinely three-marginal step not subsumed by Russell (2021), Chiba (2017), Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024), or the other two-arm results is that every two-coordinate projection of \(\mathcal U_L\) equals \(\mathcal Y_L^2\), yet the full coupling must delete exactly the triples with \(u_0>u_1\) and \(u_2>u_1\); validity therefore starts by minimizing each candidate affine slack over this non-Cartesian three-way support before tight-row ranks and facets can be classified. Duarte et al. (2024) prove a general polynomial-program representation and an anytime route to sharp discrete causal bounds; this project is informed by that framework but targets an analytic, canonical, dimension-uniform facet system. Bonet (2001) shows that causal response-type models can demand complete observable facet inequalities, providing the closest causal-polytope precedent. Avis and Fukuda (1996) show how a canonical parent forest yields duplicate-free enumeration without a visited set, which motivates the unique-predecessor requirement. Kim (2014) embeds support restrictions in a two-marginal Kantorovich dual. Gao, Ge, and Qian's (2025) arbitrary-objective multi-marginal transport identification architecture can represent the present legal-support problem after an explicit extended-cost encoding of illegal cells, but their quadratic plug-in rate does not transfer; here the equivalent finite legal-incidence linear program and its separator are proved directly. Kaido and Ponomarev (2025) characterize sharp support-restriction implications using compatibility graphs; the present non-valley support violates their regular maximal-clique correspondence and adds unique-peak coordinates. Cho and Russell (2024), Fang and Santos (2019), and Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) inform the inference handle through perturbed LP values, directional derivatives, and binding-set localization. Goodwin et al. (2022) supply a randomized three-dose setting with efficacy and adverse-event measurements from which the fixed score in \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\) could be prespecified. The proposed use is only an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis under weak individual unimodality: the trial identifies the randomized-arm score marginals but neither identifies the cross-world restriction nor clinically validates it.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The presolve proves explicit staircase facets and gives exact rational small-support certificates, but it does not construct the complete predecessor type set or an accepted source. In particular, the direct two-register implementation of alternating \(\mathrm L\) and \(\mathrm R\) staircase updates violates either fixed triangular order. The main open question must therefore produce a different representation within sixteen registers or prove that the source contract is impossible. The inference handle also leaves exact semialgebraic computation and the regular-face quantile transfer to be established.
body.honest_scope: The all-\(L\) full-facet stream, finite type theorem, transfer matrix, and adaptive exact inference are open. The finite counts \(59\), \(197\), and \(721\), the staircase family, and the three-facet projection are presolve evidence to be independently proved within the project. Under \(L=2\), the proposal must reduce to the seven-facet simplex and the middle-dose interval \([0,1/4]\) at equal Bernoulli marginals. The Goodwin et al. use case is an abstract conditional sensitivity analysis based on the prespecified score in \(\text{def:prespecified-benefit-risk-score}\). Random assignment and consistency identify its arm marginals, but the trial neither identifies nor clinically validates weak individual unimodality; no empirical verification of that cross-world restriction, clinical validation, or data analysis is claimed.
